'''Vladimir Radmanović''' ([[Serbian Cyrillic alphabet|Serbian Cyrillic]]: Владимир Радмановић; born 19 November 1980) is a Serbian former professional [[basketball]] player.

In Serbia he played for [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]] and [[KK FMP (1991–2011)|FMP]] and in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) he was a member of the [[Seattle SuperSonics]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]], [[Los Angeles Lakers]], [[Charlotte Bobcats]], [[Golden State Warriors]], [[Atlanta Hawks]] and [[Chicago Bulls]].

Radmanović also represented his [[Serbia and Montenegro men's national basketball team|national team]] most notably at the [[2002 FIBA World Championship]].

==Early life==
Radmanović was born into a Serb family in the [[East Herzegovina|eastern Herzegovinian]] city of [[Trebinje]] in [[Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina|SR Bosnia and Herzegovina]], [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|SFR Yugoslavia]] (modern [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]]) where his father Stevan (a [[Yugoslav People's Army|JNA]] colonel) was stationed at the time.<ref name="A Flight to Safety, Then a Flight to a New Life">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/03/13/sports/basketball/a-flight-to-safety-then-a-flight-to-a-new-life.html |author=New York Times |author-link=New York Times |title=A Flight to Safety, Then a Flight to a New Life |newspaper=The New York Times |access-date=2019-02-07 |date=2005-03-13 |language=en}}</ref> His family originates however from the [[Dalmatia]]n coastal town of [[Zadar]] in [[Croatia]]. Radmanović grew up in various locales dictated by the requirements of his father's profession.<ref name="A Flight to Safety, Then a Flight to a New Life"/>

==Playing career==
===Yugoslavia===
In [[Serbia and Montenegro|Yugoslavia]], Radmanović played basketball for [[KK Crvena zvezda]] and [[KK FMP (1991–2011)|KK FMP]]. During the [[NATO bombing of Yugoslavia]] in 1999, Radmanović played at the [[Nike Hoop Summit]] in [[Tampa, Florida|Tampa]] for which he was called up during the regular season.

He entered the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] in 2001.

===Seattle SuperSonics===
Radmanović was selected by the [[Seattle SuperSonics]] as the 12th pick of [[2001 NBA draft]]. Although a consistent contributor throughout his first two seasons, Radmanović became a candidate for the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award]] in the [[2003–04 NBA season|2003–04 season]]. That season he averaged 12 points and 5.3 rebounds per game mostly as a sixth man. He also established himself as an above average three-point shooter, making around 40% of his attempts, a skill that was rare for a player of his size at the time.

He was integral to the Sonics' success in the [[2004–05 NBA season|2004–05 season]] as a sixth man. He averaged 11.8 points per game and 4.6 rebounds, helping the Sonics win their first-round playoff matchup against the [[Sacramento Kings]]. On January 26, 2005, he made a career-high 8 three-point field goals against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].

After the 2004–05 season, Radmanović turned down a six-year, $42 million contract offer to re-sign with the Sonics, and instead decided to sign a one-year deal, making him an unrestricted free agent after next season.

He was nicknamed "Broadway Joe" by SuperSonics announcer Kevin Calabro, after his resemblance to NFL quarterback [[Joe Namath]].

===Los Angeles Clippers===
After voicing his frustration for not being a starter, on February 14, 2006, Radmanović was traded from the SuperSonics to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] for [[power forward (basketball)|power forward]] [[Chris Wilcox]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Clippers Acquire Radmanovic |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/radmanovic_060214.html |date=February 14, 2006 |access-date=August 15, 2009 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060830042113/http://www.nba.com/clippers/news/radmanovic_060214.html |archive-date=August 30, 2006 }}</ref>

The change of venue greatly improved his performance. Radmanović averaged 10.7 ppg, a career-best averages of 5.7 rpg and 2.1 apg, while shooting 41.8% of his three-pointers.

===Los Angeles Lakers===
[[File:Vladimir Radmanović.jpg|thumb|Radmanović with the Lakers in 2007]]
On July 13, 2006, Radmanović signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>[https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/radmanovic_sings_060713.html Lakers Sign Vladimir Radmanovic]</ref> Although he was believed to be a lock to re-sign with the Los Angeles Clippers (he at first accepted their offer at an estimated $31M over five years), he changed his mind after being promised a starting job with the Los Angeles Lakers. Although the Lakers were offering the same amount of money as Clippers, Radmanović was persuaded to join the team by [[Kobe Bryant]], [[Phil Jackson]], [[Magic Johnson]] and his good friend, [[Vlade Divac]], who were all convinced his shooting and playing opportunities would greatly increase in the Lakers' triangle offense. Jackson has also called Vladimir a "space cadet" and "my favorite Martian" in reference to his being out of position and taking wild three-point shots.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20070106173351/http://nba.aolsportsblog.com/2006/12/29/o/ More Kind Words from Phil | NBA Blog - The FanHouse]</ref> He was also referred to as "Vlad Rad."<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110520022417/http://www.pe.com/sports/basketball/lakers/stories/PE_Sports_Local_D_lakers_notes_12.3450fac.html Kobe Now on Bynum's Team | Sports | Basketball | PE.com | Southern California News | News for Inland Southern California<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> He started all 21 games in the 2007–08 Playoffs for the Lakers, and was high scorer for one game and high rebounder for several games.

====Snowboarding injury====
On February 18, 2007, Radmanović told the Lakers that he had separated his shoulder, when he fell on a patch of ice in [[Park City, Utah]], the day before, during the weekend of the [[2007 NBA All-Star Game]] and would be out for approximately eight weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/070218_radman.html |title=LAKERS FORWARD VLADIMIR RADMANOVIC SUFFERS SEPARATED SHOULDER |work=Lakers.com |date=February 18, 2007 |access-date=February 23, 2007 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070222100935/http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/070218_radman.html |archive-date=February 22, 2007 }}</ref>

However, on February 23, 2007, Radmanović revealed that he had actually hurt himself in a fall while [[snowboarding]].<ref name=LATimes>{{cite news|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-spw-lakers24feb24,1,7321581.story?coll=la-headlines-sports&track=crosspromo |title=Radmanovic lied to Lakers about injury |first=Mike |last=Bresnahan |date=February 23, 2007 |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |access-date=February 23, 2007 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080623195250/http://www.latimes.com/sports/la-spw-lakers24feb24,1,7321581.story?coll=la-headlines-sports&track=crosspromo |archive-date=June 23, 2008 }}</ref>  Radmanović's Lakers contract banned him from taking part in activities that involve significant risk of injury, including skiing and snowboarding.<ref name=LATimes/>  An NBA league source said that voiding the contract would be extremely unlikely, with a suspension or fine more likely.<ref name = LATimes/>  This proved to be true, as he was fined $500,000 for lying about the injury.

===Later NBA career===
On February 7, 2009, Radmanović was traded to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] in exchange for forward [[Adam Morrison]] and guard [[Shannon Brown]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bobcats Acquire Vladimir Radmanovic from Los Angeles Lakers |work=NBA.com |url=http://nba.com/bobcats/release_radmanovic_090207.html |date=February 7, 2009 |access-date=February 7, 2009 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210180847/http://nba.com/bobcats/release_radmanovic_090207.html |archive-date=February 10, 2009 }}</ref> Bobcats general manager [[Rod Higgins]] said Radmanović would likely play both small and power forward.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3891214 Lakers swap Radmanovic for Morrison]</ref>

On November 16, 2009, Radmanović was traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] along with [[Raja Bell]] in exchange for [[Stephen Jackson]] and [[Acie Law]].<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4659552 Warriors trade Jackson to Bobcats]</ref>

On December 9, 2011, Radmanović was signed by the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref name="nytimes">[https://web.archive.org/web/20120108000703/http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/radmanovic_pr_120911.html HAWKS SIGN VLADIMIR RADMANOVIC]</ref> In the Hawks' first game of the season on December 26, 2011, Radmanović scored 17 points with four steals and five assists in 27 minutes.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/vladimir_radmanovic/ |title=Head-to-Head ' + newstr + ' |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=July 14, 2005 |archive-date=August 17, 2005 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050817231140/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/vladimir_radmanovic/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On July 19, 2012, Radmanović signed a one-year deal with the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web | title= Bulls sign free agent forward Vladimir Radmanovic | work=NBA.com | url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-free-agent-forward-vladimir-radmanovic.html | date=July 19, 2012| access-date=July 20, 2009}}</ref> Radmanović's final NBA game was played in Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Semi-Finals on May 8, 2013, where the Bulls lost to the Miami Heat 78 - 115. Radmanović recorded 9 points, 1 assist and 2 steals in his final game. The Heat would go on to defeat the Chicago Bulls in 5 games, eliminating the Bulls from the playoffs.

In October 2013, Radmanović announced his retirement.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/report-vladimir-radmanovic-is-retiring/|title=Report: Vladimir Radmanovic is retiring|website=CBSSports.com|date=October 7, 2013 |language=en|access-date=2020-04-28}}</ref> After 12 seasons in the NBA, he appeared in 737 regular season games, shot 37.8 percent from three, and averaged 8.0 points in roughly 22 minutes per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/r/radmavl01.html|title=Vladimir Radmanović Stats|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en|access-date=2020-04-28}}</ref>

==International career==
Radmanović played for the [[Serbia and Montenegro national basketball team|senior team]] of [[Serbia and Montenegro|FR Yugoslavia/Serbia and Montenegro]] at three major tournaments.

===2002 World Championship===
Radmanović was set to debut for the senior national team at the [[EuroBasket 2001|2001 EuroBasket]] but he turned down a call-up from coach [[Svetislav Pešić]] in order to focus on preparing to enter the NBA.<ref name="Vlada Banana">{{cite news|last=Varagić|first=Bogdan|authorlink=|url=https://fosmedia.me/sport/kosarka/vlada-banana |agency=FOS Media |title=Vlada Banana |date=2019-01-13 |access-date=2022-04-07 |language=sr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190216041021/https://fosmedia.me/sport/kosarka/vlada-banana |archive-date=16 February 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Radmanović made his debut for the senior side at the [[2002 FIBA World Championship]] in [[Indianapolis]] where Yugoslavia won [[gold medal|gold]]. Radmanović (and his Seattle teammate [[Predrag Drobnjak]]) did not see many minutes at the tournament, entering the court in only three games. During half-time of the [[2002 FIBA World Championship#Semifinals 4|semifinals]] against [[New Zealand men's national basketball team|New Zealand]] in which the favored Yugoslavia was losing, coach Svetislav Pešić angrily ostracized Radmanović from the team because Radmanović was eating a [[banana]] in the change room while Pešić was giving instructions.<ref name="GJ ref">{{cite web|url=https://arhiva.glas-javnosti.rs/arhiva/2002/09/12/srpski/S02091105.shtml |last=Preradović |first=V. |agency=[[Glas javnosti]] |title=Pešićeva osveta od zlata |access-date=2026-01-05 |date=2002-09-12 |language=sr-Lat|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211208085356/https://arhiva.glas-javnosti.rs/arhiva/2002/09/12/srpski/S02091105.shtml |archive-date=8 December 2021 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Radmanović watched the rest of the game from the stands while Yugoslavia won in an uncertain finish. Radmanović didn't play in the [[2002 FIBA World Championship Final|final]] against [[Argentina national basketball team|Argentina]] either as Yugoslavia won 84–77. After the final, there was another controversy at the [[podium]] during the medal ceremony as Pešić instructed [[Aleksandar Smiljanić]] (who was on the preliminary roster but did not make the final cut) to put on Radmanović's jersey and to receive a medal instead of Radmanović. Radmanović later called the tournament a "big experience" for him.<ref name="Radmanović: Indijanapolis je životno iskustvo za mene">{{cite web |url=http://www.b92.net/sport/intervjui/intervjui.php?yyyy=2003&mm=01&nav_category=91&nav_id=80089 |author=B92 |author-link=B92 |title=Radmanović: Indijanapolis je životno iskustvo za mene |access-date=2019-02-08 |date=2003-01-02 |language=sr}}</ref>

===2004 Olympics===
Radmanović skipped out on the [[EuroBasket 2003|2003 EuroBasket]]<ref name="ESPN 2003">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/columns/story?columnist=spears_marc&id=1613923 |last=Spears |first=Marc J. |agency=[[ESPN.com]]|title=At Eurobasket, Peja's team can't deliver |access-date=2026-01-05 |date=2003-09-11 |language= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250826225548/https://www.espn.com/nba/columns/story?columnist=spears_marc&id=1613923 |archive-date=26 August 2025 |url-status=dead}}</ref> but he did take part in the [[Basketball at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Olympic tournament]] where Serbia and Montenegro was eliminated in the preliminary round.

Radmanović was coming off of an excellent [[2003–04 NBA season|season]] with Seattle and the return of [[Željko Obradović]] as national team head coach brought back enthusiasm to both players and fans alike. Radmanović played an excellent first game at the tournament, scoring 21 points against Argentina but an unbelievable last-second shot from [[Manu Ginóbili]] defeated the Serbia and Montenegro side by a score of 83–82. In the next game, Serbia and Montenegro defeated future silver medalist [[Italy national basketball team|Italy]] but the next few games after that were debacles. Namely, Serbia and Montenegro lost against New Zealand, [[Spain men's national basketball team|Spain]] and in the end against [[China men's national basketball team|China]] in the game that would have advanced them further. Radmanović's minutes and contribution decreased as the tournament progressed. Serbia and Montenegro ended up defeating [[Angola national basketball team|Angola]] in the classification game for 11th place held in [[Athens]]. The 11th-place finish was the worst in the country's Olympic basketball history.

===2005 EuroBasket===
Radmanović participated at the [[EuroBasket 2005|2005 EuroBasket]].

The 2005 EuroBasket held in [[Serbia and Montenegro]] ended up being the last international tournament Radmanović would take part in. In the deciding game against [[France national basketball team|France]], Radmanović went 4/5 from the three-point line but coach Obradović subbed him off the court when the game was being decided. Serbia and Montenegro lost that game 74–71 and bowed out of the tournament in the play-off round of the knockout stage.<ref name="I Radmanović otvorio dušu">{{cite web |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2005&mm=10&dd=16&nav_id=178482 |author=B92 |author-link=B92 |title=I Radmanović "otvorio" dušu |access-date=2019-02-10 |date=2005-10-16 |language=sr}}</ref> In four games played, Radmanović averaged 9 points and 2.5 rebounds per game. After their poor outing at the tournament, coach Obradović accused a few players for an irresponsible approach to the national team.<ref>[http://www.b92.net/sport/eurobasket2005/utakmica.php?id=26 B92.net: Eurobasket 2005]</ref>

Prior to [[EuroBasket 2007]], Radmanović said that he "won't accept a call-up only to sit on the bench and watch others play."<ref name="Radmanović dolazi ako će igrati">{{cite web |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/intervjui/intervjui.php?yyyy=2007&mm=02&nav_category=91&nav_id=233271 |author=B92 |author-link=B92 |title=Radmanović: Dolazim, ako ću igrati |access-date=2019-02-10 |date=2007-02-19 |language=sr}}</ref>
